factProposals.value: Users upload documents as plain text (.txt), CSV (.csv, either a field,value sheet or a line-items table), JSON (.json) or PDF with a text layer (.pdf), up to 10 MB; the format is decided from the file's content and must match its name.

Invoices yield invoice number, supplier, issue date, due date, currency and total (plus subtotal, tax and line items when present); contracts yield parties, effective date, end date or term, contract value, currency and renewal terms. Each value records where in the document it came from.

Documents are stored in PostgreSQL (documents table: status extracted, flagged_for_review, reviewed or rejected; fields and flags as JSON; reviewer and note); the files themselves are kept once each under their SHA-256 fingerprint, and the database holds only that reference.

A document is flagged for review, never guessed at, when a required field is missing, a date is ambiguous (e.g. 03/04/2026) or impossible, an amount or currency is unclear, two different values appear for one field, the figures do not add up, a contract has fewer than two parties, or the PDF has no text layer.

Unsupported formats (images, Office files, archives, programs) and empty or oversize files are refused with nothing stored; supported files that cannot be read (broken JSON, corrupt or password-protected PDF, read timeout) are stored and flagged; if storing a file fails, nothing is recorded as uploaded.

Flagged documents are reviewed by a compliance officer or financial analyst, never the person who uploaded them; a note is required, and an accept with corrections must pass the same checks as extraction.
A new role appears: financial analyst (from STORY-008's narrative), who reviews flagged documents alongside the compliance officer.

Every document upload, extraction outcome, review, view and refusal is in the audit log; outcomes and reviews are decisions with their rationale. Uploaders see only their own documents; to anyone else a document that is not theirs looks the same as one that does not exist.
PDFs are read with pdfjs-dist 6.4.299 or later, with script evaluation disabled: versions 5.6.83 to 6.2.107 let a malicious PDF run code (GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j).

decisions.statement: Accept text, CSV, JSON and text-layer PDFs; flag scanned PDFs as needing OCR rather than reading them.
decisions.rationale: OCR misreads amounts and dates; a wrong figure read silently is worse than a flag. Chosen by the student before building.

decisions.statement: Extract invoices and contracts, each with a fixed list of required fields.
decisions.rationale: Chosen by the student before building.

decisions.statement: Any known role may upload and see its own documents; compliance officers and financial analysts review flagged ones, never their own upload.
decisions.rationale: Chosen by the student before building; the own-upload rule keeps the reviewer independent.

decisions.statement: Refuse files that are not a supported kind, but store and flag supported files that cannot be read.
decisions.rationale: The uploader and reviewers can then see a broken invoice and why, instead of it vanishing.

decisions.statement: Keep the document's own figures when they do not add up, and flag them, rather than correcting them.
decisions.rationale: A system that silently fixes a total hides exactly what a reviewer needs to see.

decisions.statement: One document per uploader and content; the file stored once by its fingerprint.
decisions.rationale: Uploading the same file twice must not create or process it twice.

decisions.statement: Check a reviewer's corrections with the same extraction rules, by re-running extraction on the corrected values.
decisions.rationale: A review must not be a way to save values that would have been flagged.

limitations.statement: No OCR: scanned or photographed documents are flagged and must be typed in by a reviewer.

Fields are found only under a fixed list of labels (e.g. 'Total due', 'Invoice date') and invoice line items only in the form '- Description  qty x price = amount'; other layouts yield missing-field flags.
Amounts are read only in the 1,250.00 style; 1.250,00 is flagged as unreadable. A bare '$' is flagged as ambiguous.
The password-protected PDF path is tested through its error mapping, not with a real encrypted PDF.
Files are stored on the local disk; uploads are not virus-scanned.
Uploads are not yet wired into startOpsPilot() or exposed over HTTP; the service is called directly.
